output.summary: FY2026 revenue growth of 46.5% matches a roughly 46% corn price rise with flat bushels (-0.9%) and flat handling revenue. Peers with no new program grew similarly, and Cottonwood ranks only 10th of 23 on net savings growth. The auditor attributes the margin gain to inventory appreciation. So the record results are mostly a price effect, not the program. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance, which fell from $905K to $612K against a $940K budget. Other costs were flat, which points to deferred maintenance. Drying succession, safety reticence and expansion viability are untested. Defer the vote, rebuild the case on normalized prices, and do not lock in the maintenance cut.
